Exact inclusion probabilities

Source: R/psn.R
psn_inclusion_probs.Rd

Computes, without any random sampling, the probability that each pair is on a perceiver's list under psn_sample(). Use 1 / pi as the estimation weight. Arguments are the same as for psn_sample() (except seed and shuffle, which do not matter here). See inclusionprobs in SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl for what the probability does and does not cover.

Usage

psn_inclusion_probs(
  edges,
  nodes = NULL,
  consents = NULL,
  desired = NULL,
  dvals = NULL,
  carryover = TRUE
)

Arguments

edges

A data frame or matrix whose first two columns are the two endpoints of each tie (one row per tie). Values are converted to character.

nodes

Optional character vector of all node names. Only needed to include isolates, which appear in no row of edges.

consents

Optional named integer vector of consent codes, with the node names as names: 0 = none, 1 = survey only, 2 = survey and photo, 3 = photo only. Every node needs an entry. Only perceivers with code 1 or 2 receive a list, and a pair is eligible only if both nodes have code 2 or 3.

desired

Optional numeric matrix with one row per degree bin and two columns: the number of real and of counterfactual pairs to draw.

dvals

Optional list with one element per row of desired, giving the degree(s) in that bin: a single number, or a vector of consecutive degrees (e.g. 1:2) to merge several distances into one bin. Give desired and dvals together, or neither; with neither, the deployed design is used (degrees 1 to 4, five real and five counterfactual pairs each).

carryover

Whether a bin that falls short is made up from other bins.

Value

A data frame with one row for every pair that could be shown to each perceiver: perceiver, from, to, bin, real (as in psn_sample()) and pi, the probability that the pair is on that perceiver's list. Pairs outside the orbit, or in a bin beyond dvals, are not listed (probability zero).

See also

psn_sample(); the Julia package documentation, https://human-nature-lab.github.io/SamplingPerceivedNetworks.jl.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
edges <- data.frame(from = as.character(1:20), to = as.character(c(2:20, 1)))
probs <- psn_inclusion_probs(edges)
probs$weight <- 1 / probs$pi
} # }
